data.reason: Nothing has been produced and four required rungs are missing. The intent is clear enough to act on. It is a display-only change to an existing game and does not alter scoring. The first gap is the how (technical spec) and the durable what (capability contract), and neither depends on the other.
data.wave_reason: technical_spec and capability can be written side by side. The capability states observable behaviour taken straight from the INTENT: score visible during play, next to the lives, updated on dots, pellets and ghosts, scoring unchanged. The technical spec states how the existing code will surface that. Neither needs the other to exist first. dev_plan needs the spec's parts and flows to sequence work, so it waits. stories, which are only recommended, need the plan's epics. implementation needs both the spec and the contract. The intent's frontmatter says plan s13b while this plan is s13d. It reads as a leftover label and does not change what to produce.

gap.statement: There is no technical spec saying how the running score will be shown next to the lives and kept current, and no capability contract stating the in-play score display as a durable, testable behaviour. Without them there is nothing to plan or implement against.

premises.text: The INTENT asks to show the score during play next to the lives, updated as dots, pellets and ghosts are scored, with scoring itself unchanged. Today it is shown only at game end.
The LADDER lists technical_spec and capability as required and missing, and nothing has been produced yet.

artifacts.task: Read the existing game code and specify how the running score will be shown during play next to the lives. Cover where the score is already kept, where the lives display is drawn, how the display is refreshed when dots, pellets and ghosts are scored, what stays untouched (scoring rules and the end-of-game score), and how it will be tested.

Write the durable capability contract for the in-play score display, in the canon. Include the purpose and criteria a test can carry: the score is visible while the game runs, it sits next to the lives, it updates on eating a dot, a pellet or a ghost, and scoring values and the end-of-game score are unchanged. If a canon capability for the HUD or scoring already exists, extend it instead of adding a duplicate.
